blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
A serious international payments architecture is not a list of bank accounts; it is a map of flows. Money moves between entities, currencies, regions and counterparties on a rhythm that repeats every month, every week, sometimes every day. When the map is clear, treasury decisions become easy. When it is not, every new payment is a small emergency.

At the architectural level, the priorities are netting and pooling. Netting means offsetting payments between related entities so that only the net balance actually moves through a bank — reducing fees, FX costs and reconciliation load. Pooling means concentrating cash balances across entities into a single virtual pot, so that surplus in one country can fund shortage in another without a physical transfer.

Add in-house banks, intercompany loans, and a deliberate selection of correspondent banks in each region, and you have the architecture of a mature multinational treasury. None of this is visible to customers. All of it is visible to the P&L — quietly, line by line, as saved fees, faster reconciliation, and fewer painful surprises at month-end.

items.q: According to the text, a serious payments architecture is fundamentally…
items.why: "is not a list of bank accounts; it is a map of flows."

items.q: What does netting achieve, according to the passage?
options: It concentrates cash into a single virtual pot
It moves only the net balance through a bank, cutting fees and reconciliation load
It replaces correspondent banks with in-house banks
It makes payments visible to customers
items.why: "offsetting payments… so that only the net balance actually moves through a bank — reducing fees, FX costs and reconciliation load."

items.q: How does pooling let surplus in one country fund shortage in another?
options: Through a physical transfer between the two accounts
By concentrating balances into a single virtual pot, without a physical transfer
By netting the two payments against each other
By opening an intercompany loan each time
items.why: "concentrating cash balances… into a single virtual pot, so that surplus… can fund shortage… without a physical transfer."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: The benefits of a good architecture surface in the P&L over time
A well-run treasury is largely invisible to customers
Adding accounts, rather than mapping flows, is the way to build a strong architecture
Unclear flows turn routine payments into recurring emergencies
items.why: Inferência: a tese central é que a arquitetura é um mapa de FLUXOS, não uma lista de contas — o autor rejeita a ideia de somar contas.

items.q: The phrase "quietly, line by line" suggests that the savings…
options: accumulate gradually and undramatically, but do reach the bottom line
items.why: Inferência: "quietly" indica ganhos discretos e graduais que, ainda assim, aparecem no P&L.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily apresentando a redesenho de arquitetura à liderança. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you. I know a treasury slide is rarely the highlight of a leadership meeting, so let me keep this concrete. Over the next two years, this redesign will cut our cross-border bank fees by roughly a third. Not through a heroic negotiation — through architecture.

Today we run more than forty accounts across eleven entities, and almost every intercompany payment moves in full through a correspondent bank. We pay a fee, we bear the FX spread, and someone in the São Paulo team reconciles it by hand. Multiply that by a few thousand payments a month and you can see where the money goes.

What I'm proposing is a netting cycle plus a pooling structure. Instead of settling every flow gross, we offset payments between related entities once a month and move only the net. Surplus in one country funds shortage in another, inside a single virtual pot, without a physical transfer.

The catch is that none of this shows up where you'd look for a win. There's no headline, no press release. The proof is in the P&L twelve months out — lower fees, a lighter reconciliation load, and far fewer surprises at month-end. I'd rather promise you something quiet and real than something loud and fragile.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: By how much will the redesign cut cross-border bank fees, and over what period?
options: By roughly a third, over two years
By a third, over five years
By two thirds, over two years
items.why: "Over the next two years, this redesign will cut our cross-border bank fees by roughly a third."

items.q: What does Emily say is the source of the savings?
options: A heroic negotiation with the banks
Cutting the São Paulo reconciliation team
items.why: "Not through a heroic negotiation — through architecture."

items.q: What is the current problem with intercompany payments?
options: They move in full through a correspondent bank, incurring fees, FX spread and manual reconciliation
They are pooled but never settled
items.why: "almost every intercompany payment moves in full through a correspondent bank. We pay a fee, we bear the FX spread… reconciles it by hand."

items.q: What does Emily mean by "none of this shows up where you'd look for a win"?
options: The benefits are hidden from the treasury team
The gains are undramatic and appear later in the P&L, not as a visible headline
The savings go to a competitor
items.why: Inferência: ela contrasta um resultado "quiet and real" no P&L com um "headline" chamativo — o ganho não é vistoso.

items.q: What does her closing line reveal about Emily's approach?
options: She favours a dependable, understated result over a flashy but risky one
She is indifferent to whether the project succeeds
items.why: Inferência: "I'd rather promise you something quiet and real than something loud and fragile" mostra preferência pelo sólido sobre o vistoso.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We run a monthly netting cycle across the group." Netting is…
options: offsetting payments between entities so only the net balance moves
opening a new account in each currency
hedging every payment with a forward contract
auditing the bank statements line by line
items.why: Netting = compensação: abater pagamentos entre entidades e mover só o saldo líquido.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Under our ___ structure, cash from Chile can cover a gap in Poland inside one virtual pot."
items.why: Pooling = concentração de saldos num único pote virtual — excedente cobre a escassez.

items.q: "They fund the shortfall with an intercompany loan rather than a bank line." This is…
options: a loan between related entities of the same group
a loan from an external correspondent bank
an overdraft with the central treasury's bank
items.why: Intercompany loan = empréstimo entre empresas do mesmo grupo.

items.q: "A well-designed architecture cuts the reconciliation load on the desk." Reconciliation load refers to…
options: the effort of matching payments and balances to confirm they agree
the total value of cross-border payments
the number of correspondent banks in use
the FX spread paid on each transfer
items.why: Reconciliation load = a carga de trabalho de conciliar e casar pagamentos e saldos.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "An ___ acts as an internal bank for the group, lending surplus to entities that are short."
items.why: In-house bank = banco interno que funciona como banco do próprio grupo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem numa reunião de tesouraria. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the pooling structure." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the netting cycle region by region." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two regional controllers pushed back on the single virtual pot." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, questionar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed the netting calendar but never followed through." They…
options: failed to see it through to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, o oposto aconteceu.

items.q: "Renegotiating one fee schedule won't move the needle on total costs." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível — aqui, não fará.
